corrections.source_says: The syntheses covering all task types or visual tasks combine heterogeneous collective homogenization measures, including sentence-embedding comparisons and aggregates of expert ratings. Add this mixed-measure qualification to measure_detail and diversity_detail; the pooled results cannot be described solely as embedding similarity. The preprint does not specify a common embedding model or a common participant-level standard deviation.

confirmed: Read the complete 11-page PDF in memory from https://osf.io/download/wxdbt/, including references through p. 11; it has no appended supplement. Its header is 'Pre-print, 15 April, 2026'; p. 1 confirms the title and authors Alwin de Rooij and Michael Mose Biskjaer. OSF preprint metadata confirms version 1 and publication on 2026-04-21; https://api.osf.io/v2/files/69e5dc0ad6689f7079923890/ identifies the file as 'Homogenization pre-print v1.1.pdf'. The numerical verification concerns this preprint, not the later journal or conference versions.

Design_class = synthesis, context_class = synthesis, and core = no are supported: this paper conducts a systematic review and three-level meta-analysis, with no original random assignment of people. The controlled experiments summarized in Table 1 are included publications, not a new experiment conducted for this paper (pp. 3-5, Sections 3.1-3.5 and Table 1).

The corpus is 18 articles, 19 studies, and 61 effect sizes with sampling variances (p. 4, Figure 1 and Section 3.4). Table 1 lists 16 controlled and 3 quasi-experimental study entries (p. 5). These are study/effect-size counts, not people or output counts; participant totals are not reported, so n_randomized and n_analyzed appropriately remain null and the fewer-than-50-people rule is not applicable to this synthesis.

The search covered 2022 through February 25, 2026, including the first 200 Google Scholar results. Eligibility required collective semantic homogenization of creative output during or after human-AI co-creation, excluding surface-level lexical/stylistic similarity and diversity measured only within an individual (p. 3, Sections 3.1-3.2).

The reported effects are Cohen's d extracted or computed from study statistics, with one study reconstructed from original data and two from digitized graphs; positive values mean greater homogenization with AI. The preprint does not specify the SD denominator or establish that all effects use participant-level standardizers. Its model separates sampling, within-study, and between-study variance (pp. 3-5, Sections 3.4-3.5).

S1-O1 and corresponding synthesis entries match: pooled d = .334, 95% CI [.094, .574]; Q(df = 60) = 2850.50, p < .001; approximately 68% between-study and 31% within-study variance. Removing one influential study contributing three effects gives d = .247, 95% CI [.065, .429]; Q(df = 57) = 2524.19, p < .001. The publication-bias regression uses 14 peer-reviewed studies and 53 effects: b = 5.36, p = .144 (p. 6, Sections 4.1.1-4.1.3).

S1-O2 and task-specific synthesis entries match: Qm(df = 3) = 17.12, p = .002; idea generation d = 0.70, 95% CI [.30, 1.10], 5 studies/14 effects; divergent thinking d = 0.12, 95% CI [-.285, .518], 4/27; writing d = 0.27, 95% CI [-.078, .613], 9/18; visual art/design d = 0.27, 95% CI [-.555, 1.088], 2/2; Qe(df = 57) = 1860.92, p < .001 (p. 6, Section 4.2).

The divergent-thinking minus idea-generation comparison is Mdiff = -0.582, se = 0.193, p = 0.015, with 95% CI [-0.960, -0.204]; these are differences between model-implied marginal means, not an additional pooled treatment effect (p. 7, Table 2).

S1-O3 and the during/after moderator entries match: during co-creation has 8 studies/35 effects and intercept d = .453, 95% CI [.048, .953], exactly as printed despite the asymmetric interval; after-minus-during b = -.331, 95% CI [-.771, .110]; Qm(1) = 2.17, p = .141; Qe(df = 39) = 1111.59, p < .001 (p. 6, Section 4.3).

S1-O4 and the post-AI synthesis entry match: 2 studies [37, 70]/6 effects; d = .414, 95% CI [.235, .593]; Q(df = 5) = 5.75, p = .331; approximately 70% sampling and 30% within-study variance. These studies also contribute during-AI effects, and the authors call persistence tentative because of the small number of studies (p. 6, Section 4.3).

S1-O5 and the controlled/quasi-experimental synthesis entries match: controlled studies in matching writing/visual tasks, 8 studies/13 effects, d = .255, 95% CI [.034, .477]; quasi-minus-controlled b = .042, 95% CI [-.358, .442]; Qm(df = 1) = .05, p = .837; Qe(df = 18) = 1017.61, p < .001. The separate quasi-experimental analysis has 3 studies/7 effects, d = .303, 95% CI [.082, .524]; Q(df = 6) = 938.71, p < .001 (pp. 6-7, Section 4.4).

The one-line finding reproduces the preprint's overall, idea-generation, and post-AI estimates and intervals correctly (p. 6, Sections 4.1-4.3). The preprint qualifies temporal persistence and ecological validity as provisional (p. 9, Section 5.4).
summary: The April 2026 PsyArXiv preprint is a synthesis with no original randomized people study, and all recorded numerical results match its PDF. Corrections are needed to acknowledge mixed outcome measures and record the publicly linked data and analysis code.
